newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Italy to lead U.N-authorised Albania force.
newsitem.headline: Italy to lead U.N-authorised Albania force.

text.p: The U.N. Security Council on Friday authorized an Italian-led force to guard deliveries of food and other necessities in Albania as widespread violence intensified in the Balkan country.

The vote was 14 to 0 with China abstaining on a resolution that invoked Chapter 7 of the U.N. Charter which permits the use of force to protect freedom of movement for the troops in what the council called a "multinational protection force."
The mandate runs for three months at which time the council can decide whether it should be extended. It will be financed by those nations taking part, the resolution said.
The council also welcomed an offer by Italy to take the lead in organising and commanding the mission.
President Sali Berisha renewed his calls on Friday for such a forcee to be sent to his anarchic state, saying foreign police or troops were essential to safeguard aid supplies.
The humanitarian aid was seen as a key to stabilising Albania and paving the way for early elections in June.

In the countryside, a gunbattle in which 20 people were killed and the looting of an arsenal contrasted starkly with signs of a return to calm with the arrival of a first Red Cross aid truck and plans for a soccer match in Tirana on Saturday.
Berisha met an EU-led group in Tirana seeking ways to help to restore order and he was reported as saying he wanted the multinational force.

"Berisha stressed the escort of convoys of aid by police or military units of the countries Albania has asked aid from...is indispensable to provide the necessary security of this operation," an official statement by the European group said.
EU members Italy and Greece want to normalise the situation in Albania, fearing a new wave on illegal immigrants.
An Albanian boat packed with refugees capsized in heavy seas off southern Italy after a collision with an Italian navy ship and at least four people were drowned, Italian officials said.

The Italian Defence Ministry said the small Albanian coastal patrol boat, with about 30 people visible on deck, collided with the corvette Sibilla which was trying to prevent it from entering Italian waters.

Much of the south of the formerly communist country is controlled by rebels and armed gangs after protests against the collapse of savings schemes in January spilled over into insurrection in mid-March.
Greece, France, Spain, Portugal, Austria, Turkey and Romania have all expressed willingness to take part in a force to safeguard relief supplies like flour and medicines.
Police were investigating the deaths of 20 people in a shootout in the village of Frakull on Thursday, the highest toll in two months of crisis that have claimed well over 100 lives.
Villagers shot dead 17 gunmen who drove to the village and began firing weapons in the street. Three villagers were killed in the unexplained exchange, police said.
Radio Tirana said looters seized weapons from a military arsenal near the town of Gramsh after 10 hours of fighting with police.
In a sign of hope, the first Red Cross relief truck since the crisis erupted crossed into southern Albania from Greece to test perilous road routes.
